title: Purity at an unramified boundary point
statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be lisse and $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ on a
punctured smooth curve, and let $x$ be the missing point. If the
local inertia action at $x$ is trivial, then the extended stalk
$(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}$ is pure of weight $w$.

Consequently, if $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ is a dense open in a curve
in the sense of [d-real-setup] and $\mathcal G$ is a lisse Weil sheaf
on $C_0$ whose restriction $j^*\mathcal G$ is punctually $\iota$-pure
of weight $w$ on $U_0$, then $\mathcal G$ is punctually $\iota$-pure
of weight $w$ on all of $C_0$.

proof.text: Let $C_0$ be a curve as in [d-real-setup], $j:U_0=C_0\setminus\{x\}\hookrightarrow C_0$, and $\rho$ on $V=\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$ and $I_x$ be the Weil fundamental representation and the inertia group of [d-real-boundary]. If $\mathcal F$ has rank $0$ then $V=0$, the stalk below is $0$ and the claim is vacuous; assume rank at least $1$. By [lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants], $(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}\simeq V^{I_x}$, with the geometric Frobenius $F_x$ of $\kappa(x)$ corresponding to a residue Frobenius lift $\Phi$. Trivial inertia gives $V^{I_x}=V$, so the eigenvalues $\alpha$ of $F_x$ on $(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}$ are those of the invertible operator $\rho(\Phi)$; in particular $\alpha\ne0$. Purity on $U_0$ in the sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights] gives $|\iota(\alpha_y)|^2=q_y^w$ at every closed point $y$ of $U_0$, so [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] with $\beta=w$ and $S_0=\{x\}$ gives $|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_x^w$. By [lem-tw-dual-negation], the linear dual $\mathcal F^\vee$ with the contragredient Weil structure of [def-real-weil-representation-operations] is a lisse Weil sheaf of the same rank, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $-w$ on $U_0$. Its geometric generic stalk is $V^\vee$ with $g$ acting by $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\circ\rho(g)^{-1}$, so $I_x$ acts trivially on $V^\vee$ as well, and [lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants] for $\mathcal F^\vee$ identifies $(j_*\mathcal F^\vee)_{\bar x}$ with $V^\vee$, $F_x$ acting as the contragredient of $\rho(\Phi)$. By the dual clause of [p-linear-spectra] its eigenvalues are the $\alpha^{-1}$. Now [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] with $\beta=-w$ gives $|\iota(\alpha^{-1})|^2\le q_x^{-w}$, that is $|\iota(\alpha)|^2\ge q_x^w$. Hence $|\iota(\alpha)|=q_x^{w/2}$ for every eigenvalue: $((j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x},F_x)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ in the sense of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], applied with the prime power $q_x=q^{e_x}$ in place of $q$.

By [d-real-setup], $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k$ is a smooth connected curve over $k$, so by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] it is integral and every point other than its generic point $\eta$ is closed. Hence $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$, a nonempty open, contains $\eta$ and is dense, and [lem-sc-dense-open-finite-complement] makes $C\setminus U$ a finite set of closed points; its image $C_0\setminus U_0$ is a finite set of closed points. Fix $x\in C_0\setminus U_0$, and let $V=\mathcal G_{\bar\eta}=(j^*\mathcal G)_{\bar\eta}$ and $I_x$ be as in [d-real-boundary]. By [lem-a1-lisse-middle-extension] the adjunction unit $\mathcal G\to j_*j^*\mathcal G$ is an isomorphism of Weil sheaves, so it identifies $\mathcal G_{\bar x}$ with $(j_*j^*\mathcal G)_{\bar x}$ compatibly with $F_x$; by [lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants] the latter is $V^{I_x}$. A lisse sheaf has locally constant rank and $C$ is connected, so $\dim\mathcal G_{\bar x}=\dim V$; hence $V^{I_x}=V$, i.e. $I_x$ acts trivially. Put $C_0'=U_0\cup\{x\}$, open in $C_0$ since the other boundary points are finitely many closed points. Its base change is a nonempty open of the integral curve $C$, hence integral and connected of dimension one, so $C_0'$ is a curve in the sense of [d-real-setup]. For an etale neighbourhood $W$ of $\bar x$ in $C_0'$ one has $W\times_{C_0'}U_0=W\times_{C_0}U_0$, and such neighbourhoods are cofinal among those in $C_0$, so by the section formula the stalks at $\bar x$ of the ordinary direct images of $j^*\mathcal G$ to $C_0'$ and to $C_0$ agree, with the same local field and inertia. The first clause, applied to $j^*\mathcal G$ on $U_0\subset C_0'$, shows that $(j_*j^*\mathcal G)_{\bar x}\cong\mathcal G_{\bar x}$ is pure of weight $w$. Thus every eigenvalue of $F_x$ on $\mathcal G_{\bar x}$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q_x^{w/2}$, which is punctual purity at $x$ in [def-weil-punctual-weights]; points of $U_0$ hold by hypothesis.

split_report.summary: Expanded the two imported proof paragraphs. The first uses the Frobenius-equivariant inertia-invariant stalk formula, boundary semicontinuity for the sheaf and its dual, and the two weight definitions to turn reciprocal upper bounds into equality. The consequence uses finite boundary complement, locality of direct-image stalks, and the lisse middle-extension unit. No new nodes were created; the dense-open finite-complement result is cited as a generic tool. Maintainer reader repair: step 1 now cites lem-tw-dual-negation, def-real-weil-representation-operations and p-linear-spectra for the dual sheaf and reciprocal eigenvalues (def-weil-punctual-weights does not state them); step 2 derives trivial inertia from the lisse middle-extension unit, the inertia-invariant stalk formula and constant rank, and justifies that U_0 together with x is again a curve through lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings.
